lines.text: When you see a fifty-dollar shirt discounted to twenty-five dollars, are you really getting a great deal?
Retailers use a psychological mind trick called price anchoring.
The company never intended to sell that shirt for fifty dollars in the first place.
By showing you a high original price, your brain anchors to fifty dollars, perceiving twenty-five as a massive win.
Department stores also slash prices to clear warehouse inventory for incoming seasonal collections.
They often sell loss leaders—like four-dollar rotisserie chickens—at a financial loss just to get you walking past expensive items.
Never buy something just because it is on sale; buy it only if you truly need it.
